Welcome to Arirang News.
This is Key Kim.
We start with the top headlines at this hour.

1. 
Medical professors at Seoul National University Hospital begin an indefinite walkout starting Monday over an ongoing medical dispute with the government.

Professors from three affiliate hospitals including Seoul National University Bundang Hospital are also participating in the walkout.
However, an emergency committee from the hospitals emphasized that essential care would continue for patients with severe illnesses and rare diseases during the period and estimated an overall reduction in services of approximately 40 percent.

The committee instructed professors who are participating in the walkout to be present and available at the hospital during their scheduled working hours.
It also held a rally on Monday morning at Seoul National University College of Medicine which was followed by a symposium under the title "The Demise of Expert Groups."

The Korea Alliance of Patients Organization released a statement on Monday, urging the medical professors to withdraw from taking action.
The government on Sunday also announced plans to reinforce the medical emergency response system.

Based on the government's announcement, a rotational on-call system for emergency cases will be implemented starting Monday, in an effort to minimize severe medical disruptions.

2.
Samsung Electronics ranked 21st in this year's Forbes Global 2000 DOWN 7 places from last year. 

Pundits are linking the plunge in performance to lackluster semiconductor demand last year  amid the global economic doldrums.
Meanwhile, Hyundai Motor ranked  93rd, UP 11 spots from last year.
U.S. financial entity, JP Morgan Chase, ranked first for the second year in a row followed by U.S. conglomerate.. Berkshire Hathaway in second place.
Every year Forbes ranks 2-thousand global businesses by assessing their sales, assets,  and market capitalization.
?
3.
Over two years since the start of the war in Ukraine,... countries continue to look for a way to bring it to an end.
However,... at the end of the two-day Ukraine Peace Summit held in Switzerland,... a number of countries were unable to come to an agreement over the wording of a joint communique,... and decided not to sign it.

The joint communique was signed by 80 out of 93 participating countries,... and three EU institutions,... the European Parliament, the Council of the European Union and the European Commission.
Russia was not invited to the event and China did not join despite an invitation.

Among the countries that decided not to sign the joint communique were members of BRICS,... including Brazil, India, South Africa and the UAE.

However,... other major countries also decided to take a more neutral stance,... including Mexico and Indonesia.
The failure to sign comes despite the fact that the joint communique takes into account the participation of BRICS members and does not explicitly condemn Moscow for its actions.
The declaration also calls for unhindered grain exports from Ukraine, the exchange of prisoners of war, and the return of children and other civilians abducted from Ukraine to Russia.
4.
On Sunday, the Israeli military announced daily tactical pauses in fighting between the hours of 8 AM and 7 PM, local time, until further notice.

The pause applies to one of the main roads that are vital to delivering aid in Gaza,... in the area from the Kerem Shalom Crossing... to the Salah al-Din Road and northwards.

The pause during the daytime hours will help facilitate humanitarian aid to Palestinians... in areas that have been blocked since Israeli military operations in Rafah began in early May.

Outside the daily pauses, the Israeli military will continue operations in Rafah.
?
Moving to weather forecast,
After slight heat relief on Saturday, the heat is back again. Especially, those in Gangneung should notice temperatures going up nearly 5 degrees this afternoon.

It will keep getting hotter through the mid-week, with a chance of record-breaking warmth in store on Wednesday for most of Korea.

Grab your sunglasses and pack some extra water as you head outside. Sun-filled skies will boost UV rays to very high levels this afternoon except on Jeju where spotty rain is in the forecast under cloudy skies.

The medical faculty of Seoul National University 
and practitioners at its affiliated hospitals are on strike as of this Monday 
and their collective action comes a day ahead of a major walkout 
pledged by the nation's doctors for tomorrow that is Tuesday.
However, an emergency committee from the hospitals emphasized that 
essential care would continue for patients with severe illnesses 
and rare diseases during the period 
and estimated an overall reduction in services of approximately 40 percent.
The Korea Alliance of Patients Organization released a statement on Monday, urging the medical professors to withdraw from taking action.

as a means to pressure the government and criticized the walkout.

The government on Sunday also announced plans

#2
Meanwhile,
Forming trust and tailored partnerships 
are key to Seoul's journey to becoming a Global Pivotal State.
That's according to Park Jong-dae, 
Former Ambassador to South Africa and Visiting Professor 
at Yonsei University Graduate School of International Studies.
Following President Yoon Suk Yeol's three-country tour of Central Asia
last week, Park said South Korea's prowess in technology
and its development experience has helped ramp up partnerships 
in the region.
Another major achievement was establishing critical mineral partnerships
with Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, 
as South Korea’s semiconductor and battery industries 
rely on stable supplies of minerals like nickel, lithium, and tungsten.

#3
Moving on,
South Korea is ramping up efforts to boost tourism revenue.
During an economic meeting with related ministers held on Monday, 
the South Korean government said that 
it plans to introduce new visa measures and simplify entry procedures.

the government aims to draw 30 million inbound tourists 
and 30 billion U.S. dollars in tourism revenue by 2027.

the fall is due to weak performance in the semiconductor business 
caused by a global economic downturn last year.

Welcome to Arirang News			
This is Choi Jayoon.
We start with the top headlines at this hour

1
President Yoon Suk Yeol plans to ramp up South Korea's Special Strategic Partnership with Uzbekistan, through stronger cooperation in resources and infrastructure, as well as cutting-edge technology.
In a written interview with an Uzbek media outlet published Thursday, ahead of his state visit to the Central Asian country, Yoon said he aims to bolster bilateral ties to become "more mutually beneficial and future-oriented."
Since establishing diplomatic ties in 1992, South Korea and Uzbekistan have broadened the scope of their economic cooperation to include automobiles, energy, electronics, textiles, finance, and telecommunications, with bilateral trade hitting an all-time high of two-point-four-six billion last year.

2
This year's G7 Summit held in Italy, focused on a number of global issues, including the prolonged war in Ukraine.
On the sidelines of the summit on Thursday, U.S. President Joe Biden and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy agreed on a ten-year security agreement aimed at strengthening Ukraine's defense against Russia.
While the pact does not commit the U.S. to supply troops to defend Ukraine in case of an attack, it does commit Washington to hold high-level consultations with Kyiv within 24 hours if such an attack occurs.
The U.S. will also continue to train Ukraine's military, deepen cooperation on defense industry production, and share more intelligence.
The agreement also aims to help build Ukraine's long-term deterrence across multiple domains, including air, sea, and cyber security.

3
South Korea's government has vowed to take a strong stance against ‘no-show’ medical professionals as doctors and medical school professors are due to take collective action starting next week.
During an emergency briefing on Thursday, the government stated that as medical law stipulates a medical practitioner cannot refuse to treat patients without a justifiable reason, the planned walkouts would be treated as illegal acts.
Members of the Medical Professors Association of Korea, with professors at 40 universities around the country, will take a day off next Tuesday in solidarity with the Korea Medical Association in a move against the government’s medical school quota hike.
In a separate move, other major university hospitals are scheduling indefinite walkouts ? the first being professors at Seoul National University Hospital starting next Monday.

4
The Korea Economic Research Institute has raised its growth projection for the local economy this year to 2-point-4 percent from an earlier forecast of 2 percent.
Analysts there are linking the improved outlook to strong performance on the export front as semiconductor shipments surge on the back of greater AI demand.
On a more cautious note they believe recovery in domestic demand will depend on the future direction of forex markets.

5 
South Korea's economy is slowly picking up its pace.
Data from the latest economic green book from the Finance Ministry on Friday show that as inflation slows down and the manufacturing sector sees positive signs, domestic demand is growing.
For the month of May inflation was 2.7 percent on-year.
This is down from 2.9% in April.
In particular, the prices for agricultural goods have stabilized as supply improved with better weather conditions compared to the year before.
Production and construction investment also showed positive signs.
Overall industrial production for April saw an increase of 3.1% compared to the year before.
